feedback.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation for the line with the following vector equation:

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the usual formula, we get

$$
\frac{x-3}{-5}=\frac{y-0}{1}=\frac{z-(-2)}{0}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

or equivalently

$$
\frac{x-3}{-5}=\frac{y}{1}=\frac{z+2}{0},
$$

which is problematic because $\frac{z+2}{0}$ involves division by zero.

However, notice that in our line, the $z$ component always maintains the constant value of $z=-2:$

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}3-5t \\ t \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

So, in the Cartesian equation, we remove the $\frac{z+2}{0}$ part and instead write $z=-2,$ as follows:

$$
\frac{x-3}{-5}=\frac{y}{1},\,z=-2
$$
